W3 (cost lens), after E021.

**Tip (E017 code).** Muon on the conv filters, with 3 Newton-Schulz steps and filters renormalized every step, so filter wd is inert. Lookahead/EMA. Resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps. Batch 2000, widths 128/384/512, LS 0.3, SGD-group wd 0.006, 9.5 true epochs (~238 steps), max-autotune with CUDA graphs. Measured 6.548 s at 0.7537; the E019 rerun gave 6.540 s at 0.7541. My estimate of the true mean is 0.754–0.755: only about 0.1–0.2 pp above the 0.753 bar.

**Time budget:** time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction, with F ≈ 0.6 s, V ≈ 7.8 s and pixel fraction ≈ 0.755.
- Systems levers are exhausted (E015, E017 gave about 0.5% each).
- Lower-resolution steps save somewhat more than pixel-proportional (E011, E018).
- Conv MACs per sample at 32 px:
  - group 1 ≈ 93M (conv3 ≈ 33M, 7%);
  - group 2 ≈ 230M (51%);
  - group 3 ≈ 129M.
- Group 2 at 320 channels cut 7.8% of time (E021) against about 15% of MACs. FLOP cuts give back only about half their share, because fixed and elementwise costs remain.

**Exchange rates (seconds saved per pp of accuracy lost, measured against a true tip of about 0.754):**
- Epochs, −1.0 (E020): −0.69 s for about −0.12 pp, so about 6 s/pp.
- Group 2 at 320 (E021): −0.51 s for about −0.08 pp, so about 6 s/pp.
- Last-group width (E010): 1.6 s/pp.
- Dropping the 28 px phase (E018): 1.6 s/pp.
- The 20 px aggressive schedule (E011): about 0.9 s/pp.
- Epochs and group-2 width are the cheap dials, and both landed about 0.03 pp under the bar. The binding constraint is margin, not efficiency. A half-step of either (−0.5 epoch ≈ 6.2 s; group 2 at 352) is the likeliest feasible improvement. Each also costs only about 0.05 pp, so the two might combine.

**Mechanisms:**
1. Lookahead endpoint averaging is worth about +1 pp (E005).
2. Muon gives about +0.66 pp (E006).
3. Accuracy is built in the mid- and high-resolution phases. Removing resolution hurts more than its pixel share suggests (E011, E018).
4. The last group's width matters (E010). Group-2 width matters little (E021).
5. Hyperparameter nudges (LS, Muon lr, wd) all fall inside noise (E013, E014, E016/E017).
6. Kernel selection can shift the 3-seed mean by up to about 0.7 pp at identical math (E016 vs E017).

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp.
- Rebuilds can shift the mean further.
- Time noise is about 0.5–1%.
- Small accuracy deltas (<0.2 pp) cannot be resolved with one run.

**Unsure:**
- Whether the flat slopes in E020 and E021 are real or lucky draws.
- Whether group 1's depth matters on CIFAR-100.
- How much the early 20 px phase alone hurts, as opposed to E011's reduced 32 px tail.
- PCIe transfer (my guess for the 40-seed mean is ≈0.754, which is fine against 0.75).

forecasts.reason: wd nudges have all been inside noise and this one leaves time unchanged; a +0.2 pp gain over E016's 0.7607 is very unlikely.
7% of MACs, plus its elementwise traffic, likely gives back about 6–8% of time, borderline against the 8% bar; removing depth at full resolution probably costs about 0.2–0.4 pp.
Pixel fraction drops only about 0.026, so the saving is about 0.2–0.27 s (≈3.5–4%), borderline against the 4% bar; the early phase is cheap in accuracy, with a loss of about 0.1 pp.

cruxes: Is the tip's true mean about 0.754, giving only about 0.1 pp of usable margin, or higher? This decides whether a −0.5 epoch trim or group 2 at 352 (≈6.2–6.3 s) clears 0.753.
Are the flat accuracy slopes in E020 and E021 (about 0.1 pp per 0.5–0.7 s) real? If so, combining half-steps of epochs and group-2 width beats any resolution or depth trick.
Does the 20 px early phase cost almost no accuracy (≤0.1 pp)? If so, it adds about 0.25 s of nearly free savings that stack with the epoch trims.
